log.why: E9 splits the prior probability mass roughly in half (0.545 vs 0.455), maximizing expected information gain for Ticket 1.
Treating at 3 µM bisects the threshold prior mass (0.488 for <= 3 µM vs 0.512 for > 3 µM) for maximum information.
Testing the leading candidate lacZ directly can confirm it for immediate publication or narrow down to fliC and hisG.
E2 (1 uM) splits the remaining probability mass in Ticket 2 (~56% vs ~44%) and isolates the 3 uM hypothesis if negative.
E1 directly tests the leading hypothesis hisG (0.501) and distinguishes it from the runner-up fliC (0.340).
Treating at 10 µM splits Ticket 3's prior probability mass nearly in half (0.531 vs 0.469) for maximum information gain.
hisG has a 0.919 posterior probability and time is running low on Ticket 1.
Test 30 uM on Ticket 3 to split its top hypotheses while we still have time to publish Ticket 2 during incubation.
3 µM has a strong 0.670 posterior after response at 3 µM and no response at 1 µM, with little time left.
E5 splits the prior probability nearly in half by testing the top candidate ompF alongside katG while leaving time to publish Ticket 3.
Two assays bracketed the threshold at 30 µM with 0.749 probability, which is high enough to publish before time runs low.
Ticket 4 is urgent with 34s left; testing the leading candidate dnaK (0.435) directly can confirm it for immediate publication.
Test the leading hypothesis araC on Ticket 5 while waiting 6 seconds for Ticket 4's E3 result.
With only 8 seconds left, publishing the leading hypothesis araC (0.410) has positive expected value and avoids expiration penalty.
E9 tests half the posterior mass (dnaK, araC, rpoB = 0.476) to quickly narrow down the culprit gene before the round ends.
Test {rpoB, recA} in parallel with E9 to distinguish the top four candidates before round time expires.
